findings.title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unhandled RuntimeException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by regex-replacing the locale and community path in the absolute path, then throws a raw RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only translates IOException from reading the target file into MojoExecutionException, so a properties file with no matching _en counterpart (or a path the regex does not rewrite as expected) crashes the whole verifier run with a stack trace instead of producing a per-file verification message or checking the remaining files.

findings.title: Anchor pattern matches non-anchor tags and misses uppercase anchors
findings.body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>' with no word boundary and no case-insensitivity. It therefore treats tags such as <abbr>, <article> or <address> as anchors and can strip them from the checked value when they happen to match the English string, bypassing the HTML policy for elements that were never intended to be whitelisted. Conversely a legitimate <A HREF=...> anchor identical to the English source is not recognised, is left in the value and is then reported as illegal HTML. The pattern needs a boundary after 'a' (and case-insensitive matching) to represent anchor tags only.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch message identifies neither the key nor the file
findings.body: When a translated anchor does not match the English source, santizeAnchors() adds only "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Unlike the Illegal HTML message it omits the message key and the file being verified, so when the plugin checks hundreds of properties files in CI the maintainer cannot locate the offending entry from the build output without re-running or searching manually.

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian sentence was replaced while removing its anchor tags, apparently by copying the corresponding Italian string, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. As with the account bundle, removing the FreeOTP/Google Play anchors replaced the Lithuanian translation with the Italian sentence, so the login TOTP instructions will be shown in the wrong language.

findings.title: No positive test that legitimate HTML and matching anchors pass
findings.body:
All new tests only assert that a violation is reported (illegal tag, HTML where English has none, changed anchor). There is no fixture asserting an empty result for a translation that reuses exactly the English string's allowed HTML (

//
) and identical anchor, nor for the special-case normalisations (choice formats, templateHelp). A regression that flags every HTML-containing translation would still pass the whole suite while breaking the verifier for the real message bundles.
